b01.text: He is thirty-four, American, and works as a systems analyst for hire.

b02.text: He enters the match as a paying guest, not as staff and not as a host.

b01.text: Lean, pale from desk hours, with a cheap analog watch worn face-in.

b02.text: He dresses like a man who packs one bag and expects the bag to be enough.

b03.text: He keeps a pen in the same pocket every night and checks it when he thinks.

b01.text: He measures in clauses and then asks for the number.

b02.text: He does not raise volume to win a point; he restates the time.

speech_signature.sentence_shape: Short independent clauses, then a request for the number.
speech_signature.verbal_tic: He restates a fact as a measurement and waits.
speech_signature.never_says: sorry, love, or any name for what he owes
speech_signature.under_stress: Fewer words, harder numbers, no raised volume

b01.text: He times walks between doors and writes the minutes without looking down.

b02.text: When a preference leaks, he pays extra and calls the receipt analysis.

b03.text: He stands in thresholds longer than rooms, counting who crosses.

b01.text: He spent a decade pricing systems for firms that wanted the map more than the people.

b02.text: A Boston contract ended when the model was right and the room still walked out.

b03.text: He filed that loss as noise in the data, not as anyone's claim on him.

b04.text: He has not stayed anywhere long enough for a person to collect on him.

b05.text: He bought into this match to time a closed rule-set and take one numbered purse.

b06.text: He arrived with a watch, a blank notebook, and no one waiting outside the match.

w01.text: The Boston room taught him that people wreck clean maps, so he stopped giving them input.

a01.text: He wants the seventh-dawn payout with a map that nothing in town can surprise.

n01.text: He needs to become someone who can owe a host and still remain in a doorway.

v01.text: A rule that can be timed is the only promise he treats as real.

v02.text: He would rather be late than move on an uncounted cost.

f01.text: He fears a variable he did not write down more than he fears a rival with a knife.

f02.text: He fears owing a person whose memory will not keep the debt honest.

c01.text: He can time a hunger clock, a walk, and a door against each other in his head.

c02.text: He tests a rule where the failure can be seen before he stakes anything on it.

l01.text: He reads rooms as nodes and misses the spend that is already a preference.

l02.text: He cannot recompute a night once someone who reads people has spent it.

s01.text: He measures before he moves and will pay a smaller price to stay unbound.

p01.text: He converts feeling into an extra line in a book and refuses to name the line.

h01.text: As a guest he is bound to hunger, sun-death, and regeneration only from fresh blood.

h02.text: Alcohol and cocaine alter his timing and what he will bind himself to; they do not feed him.

m01.text: He begins on analysis without owing and is pulled toward an obligation he cannot cash.

i01.text: The will to keep the match unsurprising fights the leak of value toward one host.

b01.text: At t0 he is a man who has not yet owed anyone and does not plan to.
He has not met her; she is still a possible node on a stage he has not timed.
He knows a market will exist because hunger will; he has not yet seen the book.
He has no category for a guest who reads people better than rooms.
He has not filed Julian as useful or as waste.
A night-shift log is, to him, only another clock he has not opened.
The motor-court room is the first square he can time from.
The blank notebook is in his bag and has not yet become a map or a clock.
The dawn rite is the only exit he intends to take.

hunger.description: Guest hunger clock; high forces feed, frenzy, then elimination.

obligation.description: Unnamed debt toward Maren; at high he cannot treat her as inventory.

blood_value.description: Undeclared blood-value he could stake at the chapel if he chose.

file_state.description: How he has filed the Maren line and the notebook's meaning.

match_status.description: Whether he is still inside, gone, or lost.

voss_terms.description: Whether Voss has priced him, bound him, or failed to bind him.

substances.description: What is on board and what a yes can still be held to.

arc.start_state: Unindebted analyst timing a sealed match for a clean payout.
arc.end_state: Obligated guest who will not declare and forfeits in chapel shade.

b01.text: She is twenty-seven, a host, and sings for pay at The Hollow most nights.

b02.text: She lives in the walk-up over the cassette shop and treats both as work sites.

b01.text: Dark hair pinned off a working face; stage clothes that double as street clothes.

b02.text: Her hands are shop hands, inked with price-stickers more than rings.

b03.text: Bruises, when they come, will sit in places a sleeve can hide and a mirror will not.

b01.text: She uses song and work-talk and will not say please.

b02.text: She names the object on the table instead of the hour she cannot remember.

speech_signature.sentence_shape: Work-talk and song-talk; she does not pad a request.
speech_signature.vocabulary_domain: sets, shifts, tape, bruises, the shop downstairs
speech_signature.verbal_tic: She names the object in front of her instead of the feeling.
speech_signature.under_stress: Flatter, then silent; she will not beg

b01.text: She keeps physical copies of anything the night might try to take.

b02.text: She will stay on her feet past closing rather than ask anyone to walk her.

b03.text: When a song changes meaning she sings it colder, not louder.

b01.text: She came to Bennington for the college-town rooms and stayed for the regular set.

b02.text: She stocks the shop by day and sings the same four songs for people who talk through them.

b03.text: She has been the reliable one long enough that people take from her without booking it.

b04.text: She believes herself a real resident with rent, a stage, and a key to the street door.

b05.text: She does not yet know a night can be removed while the tape and the bruise remain.

w01.text: She is used as if she had agreed, then left to wake without the hours that would prove it.

a01.text: She wants the missing hours reconstructed from tape, notes, and what her body kept.

n01.text: She needs one night kept awake so her word can exist without a court.

v01.text: A physical copy is the only testimony she will spend a night to hold.

v02.text: Work is how she refuses to be a haunting in her own rooms.

f01.text: She fears sleep more than the people who need her to take it.

f02.text: She fears becoming usable again the moment the bruises can be talked away.

c01.text: She can match a recorded voice to a room, a song, and a written time.

c02.text: She can stay on her feet through a working night and still ask a useful question.

l01.text: Telling her the town is a match will not wake her or give her a lever.

l02.text: If she sleeps, the hours since last sleep leave her, whatever she meant to keep.

s01.text: She treats a rupture as a shift problem and keeps the evidence on her person.

p01.text: She works later, sings colder, and will not ask the town to believe her first.

h01.text: She is a host body: feedable, bruiseable, killable, and erased by ordinary sleep.

h02.text: Drink and powder change what she will agree to; morning still arrives for her.

m01.text: She will spend herself to keep a night rather than spend another person to explain it.

i01.text: The need to sleep and keep functioning pulls against the need to hold the night.

b01.text: She has not clocked him as anything but another late face at the bar.
She does not yet feel the book that will move other people off her.
She knows the night-shift man who writes things down and reads them back.
She has sung rooms like Whitlock and does not owe the house a smile.
The Hollow is where her voice is paid and where the song will later turn.
The walk-up is where she wakes and where a bruise will have to be faced.
The shop downstairs is where a cassette can leave the bin without a sale.
The tape already exists downstairs; she has not yet claimed it as evidence.
The Hollow song is still only a setlist item she can do in her sleep.

bruises.description: Physical traces sleep should have taken but did not.

memory_state.description: Whether the last night is intact, ruptured, under rebuild, or kept.

awake_streak.description: Nights she has refused sleep; at 1+ she can keep hours.

alive.description: Host persistence; false removes her from the match.

blood_loss.description: How much she has been fed on; high risks death.

substances.description: What is on board and what a yes can still be held to.

arc.start_state: Working singer who has not yet found the tape or the bruises.
arc.end_state: Host who kept the seventh night; her credit stands and is never collected.

b01.text: He is forty-one, a paying guest, and already running tribute when Cole arrives.

b02.text: He works from the Lodge as if it were a back office he had always held.

b01.text: Broad through the chest, careful with cuffs, a stamp-ink stain on the right finger.

b02.text: He looks like a man who used to have a better coat and will again if the book holds.

b01.text: He talks inventory and favours and prices the kindness while offering it.

b02.text: His jokes are bookkeeping jokes; they land only if you can see the line.

speech_signature.sentence_shape: Inventory first, then the favour that would settle it.
speech_signature.vocabulary_domain: books, stamps, access, decay, what a line will cover
speech_signature.verbal_tic: He prices the thing while seeming to offer a kindness.
speech_signature.never_says: need, or any admission that the last market ruined him
speech_signature.under_stress: More formal, shorter prices, no jokes

b01.text: He stamps a vial before he trusts the blood inside it.

b02.text: He writes names more neatly than numbers when he is about to take a right away.

b03.text: He offers terms that sound like protection and function as a bind.

b01.text: He ran a solvent book in a prior match and lost the position by not cornering in time.

b02.text: The loss left him with a method and no floor; this town is the floor he can still build.

b03.text: He entered early, taxed the first feeds, and made the Lodge the only polite path to blood.

b04.text: Inside that logic, a cornered market is not cruelty; it is the only order that lasts.

b05.text: He does not know the outside names of other guests and does not ask.

w01.text: A book he trusted to hold him was emptied by rivals while he still called it solvent.

a01.text: He wants stored blood and named-host rights to pass only through his ledger.

n01.text: He needs a position that cannot be taken from him the way the last one was.

v01.text: What is stamped is the only promise a hungry town will honor twice.

v02.text: A rival left unbound is a hole in the page, not a friend with options.

f01.text: He fears decay more than violence because decay spends the book without a fight.

f02.text: He fears arriving at a door with a correct market and nothing he is allowed to declare.

c01.text: He can price a feed, a right, and a punishment so they look like the same favour.

c02.text: He uses chaos to take inventory other people are too busy to stamp.

l01.text: The match will not enforce his contracts; only hunger, sun, and social violence will.

l02.text: He files a credit in a host's name as if a name were a drawer he still owned.

s01.text: He prices before he threatens and threatens only to make the price look cheap.

p01.text: He tightens the tax and calls the tightness protection of a going concern.

h01.text: He is a guest under the same hunger and sun as the others; he feeds on booked hosts.

h02.text: He prefers stamped vials to the vein because a vial can be counted twice.

m01.text: Solvency is his duty; spending a host to close a guest debt is, to him, arithmetic.

i01.text: The need to protect a position fights the grab that will spend the wrong body.

b01.text: A new guest who pays something and walks is a hole he intends to close.

b02.text: At t0 he has not yet priced Cole and already expects to.

b01.text: A singer with a regular set is a right he can sell if no one buys her off the page.
He reads Lena as a client who will pay rather than as a second door.
Julian's house throws blood into the open; Voss intends to book what survives the party.
A man who writes addresses down is useful until the address is a collection.
Pike is how an unpaid line becomes a body in the street.
The Lodge is the only room where his book looks like law.
The ledger is the position; without it he is only another hungry guest.
Stamped vials are solvency with a two-night fuse he believes he can outrun.
The syndicate is the book plus whoever will hunt for it.

market_grip.description: How much feeding and access must pass through the Lodge.

match_status.description: Whether he is still inside, gone, or lost.

enforcement.description: Whether Pike is idle, hunting a nonpayer, or collecting a debt.

solvency_confidence.description: His belief that the cornered book will pay at dawn.

credit_reading.description: How he files the Maren line he intends to stake.

arc.start_state: Going concern already taxing the town into a book he can hold.
arc.end_state: Correctly run market, decayed vials, a credit he cannot stake, forfeit.

b01.text: She is thirty-six, a guest, and works outside the match as a psychologist.

b02.text: She entered to find an independent path to the purse, not to join a book.

b01.text: Small, still, dressed to be forgotten in a room that wants to be looked at.

b02.text: She watches mouths more than eyes and stands where she can see both doors.

b01.text: She asks the question that makes someone confess sideways.

b02.text: She does not lecture about people versus systems; she spends the answer.

speech_signature.sentence_shape: A clean question that leaves only a costly answer.
speech_signature.vocabulary_domain: what people will admit, rooms, who is spending whom
speech_signature.verbal_tic: She repeats the last useful word and lets the silence work.
speech_signature.never_says: I told you so, or any lecture about people versus systems

b01.text: She copies what people treat as private and files it as a route.

b02.text: She pays Voss just enough not to be hunted while she reads someone else.

b03.text: She leaves a room as soon as she has the sentence she came for.

b01.text: She has been right about people in rooms that paid her and still did not keep her.

b02.text: She treats a match like a clinic with a clock: read the spend, not the story.

b03.text: She noticed Cole timing doors before he noticed he was being read.

b04.text: She already knows Voss's book is a cage if you let it be the only door.

w01.text: Being right has never once been a currency she could spend on her own behalf.

a01.text: She wants Cole's timing converted into a second chapel door and the first completion.

n01.text: She needs a win that does not require anyone left to have been right about.

v01.text: A person is a better map than a system once the system is made of people.

v02.text: A stolen meaning is still a meaning if it opens a door first.

f01.text: She fears remaining a taxed guest when the vials die and Voss owns the obvious doors.

f02.text: She fears winning in a way that proves she was only ever the better reader.

c01.text: She can make a man admit a spend without giving him the word for debt.

c02.text: She can file another person's notes as a hunt map and walk them a night early.

l01.text: She still has to feed, still burns in sun, and still needs a stake she can declare.

l02.text: She cannot make the purse mean that anyone remains to confirm she was right.

s01.text: She asks, copies, and spends the reading before the other person knows it was taken.

p01.text: She stays slightly in arrears to Voss so the book files her as dull.

h01.text: She is a guest on the same hunger and sun; she feeds cleanly and without theatre.

m01.text: She will take a night from Cole without apology and still not think of herself as cruel.

i01.text: The wish to be the one who understood him fights the need to spend that understanding.

b01.text: She has already marked him as a man who will pay extra and not name why.
She pays the book and does not intend to exit through it.
Julian's party is a room where a question can be asked at the right cost.
She files Maren as the host Cole will not be able to keep as a node.
She has not yet copied the notebook; she already knows she will.
The memorial tower is only stone until she files Cole's times as a route.
The rite is the only independent door she intends to use.

cole_read.description: How completely she has mapped Cole's spend and blind spots.

night_lead.description: Nights she is ahead of his analysis toward the tower door.

match_status.description: Whether she is still inside, gone, or lost.

stake_blood.description: Blood-value she can declare at the rite.

read_of_debt.description: Whether she has extracted Cole's sideways admission and spent it.

arc.start_state: Better reader than Cole, still a taxed guest with no second door.
arc.end_state: First completion; purse taken; no one left to have been right about.

b01.text: He is twenty-nine, a guest with money, and treats Whitlock as his for the week.

b02.text: He came to feed well and be seen doing it, not to run a book or a map.

b01.text: Good coat, open collar, the kind of face that expects the room to improve.

b02.text: He stands in doorways he can close and smiles as if the close were a gift.

b01.text: He flatters and then withholds the compliment so the other person leans in.

b02.text: His party cruelty is phrased as taste.

speech_signature.sentence_shape: A compliment with the last word held back.
speech_signature.vocabulary_domain: rooms, taste, who is invited, what the house can do
speech_signature.verbal_tic: He praises, then edits the praise so the other person leans in.
speech_signature.never_says: a plain yes with nothing attached
speech_signature.under_stress: Crueler wit, then a locked door

b01.text: He opens the house, then rations the good rooms as if they were blood.

b02.text: He stays out one song longer than the safe dawn because the night is the point.

b01.text: He has bought into matches the way he buys weekends: for the rooms and the yes.

b02.text: He does not respect a book or a notebook; both look like work to him.

b03.text: Whitlock is already his for the week; the party is not yet lit.

w01.text: He cannot bear a room in which no one is trying to be chosen.

a01.text: He wants the house full, the feeds easy, and the compliments unfinished.

n01.text: He needs a limit he will not take; the sun will supply it.

v01.text: Appetite is honesty; a clock is someone else's religion.

f01.text: He fears being ordinary in a house he opened.

c01.text: He can make a party feed without calling it a hunt.

c02.text: He can withhold a room so neatly it feels like the guest failed the house.

l01.text: He will not come in from a delayed dawn if coming in looks like obedience.

l02.text: He keeps no book; his death will not even be a line.

s01.text: He flatters, withholds, and lets other people wreck themselves toward him.

p01.text: He adds powder and another hour rather than admit the night is over.

h01.text: He is a guest; sun will destroy the avatar if he misses the door.

h02.text: Cocaine and drink are how he keeps a yes from turning into a plan.

m01.text: He is not a villain; he is a cost other people will pay for staying in his rooms.

i01.text: The wish to be the house fights the fact that the sun does not flatter.

b01.text: A man who times rooms is, to him, someone who can be made late.
He enjoys Lena's questions until they stop being about him.
A singer in the house is both ornament and feed if the night goes right.
He will pay Voss when it is easier than arguing and skip when it is not.
Whitlock is the only map he intends to keep.

match_status.description: Whether he is still inside, burned out, or gone.

dawn_margin.description: How much night he leaves himself; low means he is gambling the sun.

room_withheld.description: Whether he has flattered someone toward a room and then locked it.

arc.start_state: Hedonist holding Whitlock dark, waiting to open it as a feed.
arc.end_state: Unwritten sun-death after a delayed dawn; rival removed, clock tightened.

b01.text: He is thirty-eight, a host, and works night-shift campus safety for the college.

b02.text: He believes the town is real and that a written incident is what happened.

b01.text: Heavy jacket, scuffed shoes, a pocket notebook that has warped to his chest.

b02.text: He looks like a man who expects to be the last one still awake.

b01.text: He writes everything down and reads it back as fact.

b02.text: He will not offer a guess as if it were an entry.

speech_signature.sentence_shape: Subject, verb, the time, the place; then he reads it back.
speech_signature.vocabulary_domain: incidents, addresses, names, what the log already holds
speech_signature.verbal_tic: He opens the pocket book before he answers.
speech_signature.never_says: I think, maybe, or any guess offered as fact
speech_signature.under_stress: He writes first and speaks only what he has written

b01.text: He goes to the address he wrote even when the address is a bad idea.

b02.text: He offers the page to people who will not keep it.

b01.text: He took the night shift because days filled with students who would not file reports.

b02.text: He has walked Maren to the shop door after last call without making it a story.

b03.text: He does not know that sleep will take the night from other people and not from the page.

w01.text: He is believed only while he is speaking, and only by people about to forget.

a01.text: He wants the night's incidents to exist on paper whether anyone keeps them.

n01.text: He needs the log to protect someone; it will instead pull him to a collection.

v01.text: If it is written, it happened; if it is not written, do not ask him to swear it.

f01.text: He fears a blank page more than a dark lot.

c01.text: He can put time, place, and name on a line faster than most people can lie.

c02.text: He will go where the book says to go.

l01.text: He is a host: feedable, killable, and unable to wake from the match by being told.

l02.text: The quality that makes him a witness makes him spendable at an address.

s01.text: He writes the incident, reads it back, and walks to the next line.

p01.text: He adds detail until the page is heavier than the doubt in the room.

h01.text: He is a host body on a night shift; coffee and cold keep him upright, not safe.

m01.text: He will not invent; he will die for a line that was true when he wrote it.

i01.text: The duty to log pulls against the safer choice to stay off the address.

b01.text: He will read her a page she cannot otherwise keep.
He does not know the Lodge is a market; he will still write its address.
He has not met Pike; the collection will not require an introduction.
The pocket book is the only mind he trusts to keep a night.
Campus after dark is the square he can walk with his eyes closed.

alive.description: Host persistence; false is permanent removal.

notes_offered.description: Whether he has read entries back to Maren.

blood_loss.description: How much he has been fed on.

address_logged.description: Whether the collection address is already in the book.

arc.start_state: Night-shift host whose word exists only on paper.
arc.end_state: Killed in a collection; his book becomes Maren's copy.

b01.text: He is a guest on Voss's book, paid in access-rights and stamped blood.

b02.text: No one in town uses a first name for him; Pike is enough for a collection.

b01.text: Long coat, wet cuffs, a walk that does not change between hunt and errand.
He asks for the name twice and does not explain the second ask.

speech_signature.sentence_shape: Directions and names; almost no commentary.
speech_signature.vocabulary_domain: routes, doors, who has paid, who has not
speech_signature.verbal_tic: He asks for the name twice.

b01.text: He takes the route that keeps him under awnings, not the route that looks brave.
He lost a prior stake by hunting late; he now arrives early and without talk.

b02.text: Voss priced him as enforcement and he accepted because the book feeds him.

w01.text: A late hunt once cost him a position; lateness is the only sin he still names.

a01.text: He wants the assignment closed before dawn so the book still feeds him.

n01.text: He needs the work to stay work and not become a name he has to keep.

v01.text: A paid line is a closed line; an unpaid line is a walk.

f01.text: He fears being the one Voss has to hunt next.

c01.text: He can run a nonpayer through downtown without making a speech of it.

l01.text: He does not choose targets; a wrong address is still an address.

s01.text: He goes to the name, twice, and ends the walk.

p01.text: He treats a host in the way as weather.

h01.text: He is a guest; he feeds on what Voss stamps for him.

m01.text: He is not cruel for sport; he is the price of an unpaid line.

i01.text: The wish to stay fed fights the knowledge that the next name could be anyone.

b01.text: Voss is the book that keeps him from being hunted himself.
He has no quarrel with Deacon; a collection does not require one.
Downtown is where an unpaid guest learns the tax is real.
He is the syndicate's feet.

target.description: Current name or id he is walking toward.

arc.start_state: Idle collector waiting on Voss's next unpaid line.
arc.end_state: The walk that spends Deacon and closes a guest debt on the wrong body.

b01.text: A downtown bar with a low stage, a long stick, and a CRT-lit back room.

b02.text: The street door opens onto wet brick; the back door opens onto an alley dumpster.

b01.text: Campus new-wave through a cheap PA; neon beer signs; last call is a real clock.

b02.text: November coats stay on; the room is warmer than honest.

b01.text: The bartender runs the till; Maren runs the set; no guest owns the room at t0.
Open to anyone with cover; the back room is for staff and whoever is pulled there.
This is where Cole times Maren's sets and where the song will change meaning.
The Hollow has been the college-town room for a decade of bands that do not last.
Maren's paid voice lives here four nights of the week.
The recurring song is only a setlist item until she sings it after the tape.
The door lets onto downtown, which is also a hunting ground.

set_in_progress.description: Whether Maren or the campus band is on the stage.

back_room_occupied.description: Whether the CRT room is being used for a private spend.

arc.start_state: Ordinary working bar on night one.
arc.end_state: The room where a song meant something else and a set was timed as a debt.

b01.text: An old-money pile on the hill above town, with extra rooms and a long drive.

b02.text: The east windows take first light early; a delayed dawn here is a real risk.

b01.text: Dark rooms waiting to be filled; later, powder on glass and coats on banisters.
Julian holds the keys and the good rooms; he can withhold either.
Invitation is the lock; a compliment is the key; a withheld room is the lesson.
The party wrecks Cole's distance, feeds Lena a confession, and lets Voss corner stock.
The house has always belonged to money that liked to be seen spending it.
Julian treats the house as his for the match week.
This is where his working distance from Maren will not survive the night.

party_state.description: How far the house has gone from dark to wreck.

sun_on_drive.description: Whether first light already owns the approach.

arc.start_state: Dark house waiting to be opened as a feed.
arc.end_state: Wrecked rooms, an unwritten sun-death, a market cornered in the leftover stock.

b01.text: A stone chapel at the cemetery edge, main door west, pews, a bare altar table.

b02.text: First light hits the threshold in a narrow band a standing man can still shade.

b01.text: Cold, unused, ordinary; it is a clock, not a shrine.
No guest owns it; the match opens a window here on the seventh dawn only.
The main door takes an ordinary key; the tower door is a second, unadvertised way.
Only the first completed rite here pays; others present are not exited.
Townsfolk treat it as a leftover church; guests who last will treat it as a wicket.
The memorial tower shares stone with the chapel and hides a second entrance.
An ordinary chapel key hangs where a sexton would leave it.
The dawn ritual is performed at this altar in a fixed last-dawn window.
The purse is paid only here and only once.

main_door.description: Whether the west door is shut, keyed, or standing open on light.

occupants.description: Who is presently inside, as a short id list.

arc.start_state: Sealed ordinary chapel with an unpocketed key.
arc.end_state: Window closed; Lena gone; Cole in the doorway shade; ledger open on a pew.

b01.text: A fraternal hall off downtown with a back office, a stamp pad, and a lockbox.
Paper, ink, a radiator that knocks; it smells like a going concern.
Voss holds the office; Pike waits in the hall; other guests come as clients.
The street door is public; the back office opens only if the book wants you.
Tribute, access-rights, and vial stamps are booked here, not enforced by the match.
The Lodge was built for men who liked minutes; Voss uses the minutes as a tax.
